subject.title: fix(polls): add default maximum poll option count

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally reject Matrix polls above 20 answers even though the upstream SDK permits the array and major clients may truncate rather than reject such events?
rationale: The patch changes existing user-visible behavior based on an interoperability convention rather than a demonstrated protocol or dependency hard limit, so product compatibility intent cannot be inferred safely from code alone.

options.title: Preserve permissive behavior
options.body: Do not add the hard limit until an authoritative upstream contract or a separately sponsored OpenClaw policy establishes that rejection is desired.

options.title: Adopt fail-closed 20
options.body: Explicitly accept the compatibility change, retain Matrix-owned enforcement, and require documentation plus live fresh-install and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Normalize excess answers
options.body: Send only the first 20 answers with explicit user-visible feedback, avoiding a hard failure but intentionally changing the submitted poll content.

recommendation.title: Preserve permissive behavior
recommendation.body: Do not add the hard limit until an authoritative upstream contract or a separately sponsored OpenClaw policy establishes that rejection is desired.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Matrix QA ownership makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the channel-specific interoperability choice.
